narrativeReportMd:
# SubstanceReferenceInformation R4-to-R6 breaking-change assessment

## Bottom line
`SubstanceReferenceInformation` is a hard R4-to-R6 break because the R6 core package has no same-name or same-canonical resource. Existing R4 instances with `resourceType: "SubstanceReferenceInformation"` will not validate as R6 core resources, and generated R6 models are unlikely to expose the R4 class.

## Scope
I compared the R4 StructureDefinition against the R6 package index and searched the R6 package for an exact counterpart. Because no counterpart exists, I reviewed `SubstanceDefinition` and `Substance` as likely substance-domain successors but did not treat them as a confirmed rename.

## Main migration themes
The migration issue is primarily artifact identity and conversion, not a local cardinality or terminology tightening on the same element. R4 local content (`comment`, `gene`, `geneElement`, `classification`, and `target`) has no lossless same-path home in R6. Some information may be manually remodeled into `SubstanceDefinition`, but candidate paths differ in meaning, requiredness, and type choices.

## Highest-impact findings
The highest-impact finding is removal of the resource identity itself. A secondary high-impact risk is data loss or semantic drift when attempting to map the R4 local content model into `SubstanceDefinition`.

## Findings requiring human review
Human review is needed to decide whether a project should map records to `SubstanceDefinition`, preserve them with extensions, keep them in an R4 compatibility store, or reject them as retired trial-use content.

## Backward-compatible design observations
A less disruptive design would have kept a deprecated R6 shell or provided an official cross-version mapping. The R4 artifact was immature and under-specified, so removal may be justified, but the supplied package inputs do not include the rationale.

## Follow-up analysis
Review the broader substance model redesign, especially `SubstanceDefinition`, and obtain any official cross-version ConceptMap or ballot notes before implementing automated conversion.

summary.executiveSummaryMd: `SubstanceReferenceInformation` has a hard breaking R4-to-R6 identity change: the R6 core package does not define the resource. The top migration concerns are invalid R6 resourceType values, generated-model/API removal, and lack of a lossless mapping for `gene`, `geneElement`, `classification`, and `target` content. The main uncertainty is whether HL7 intended a specific `SubstanceDefinition` mapping outside the supplied computable package files.
summary.migrationThemesMd: Treat this as a removed trial-use resource rather than a simple rename. Systems with stored R4 data need an explicit migration policy: keep the data in R4 form, map selected content to `SubstanceDefinition` with manual rules, or preserve unmapped content in extensions. Any automated transform should be tested for resource identity, local backbone content, candidate `target`/`relationship` mappings, and round-trip loss.
summary.confidenceSummaryMd: Confidence is high that the same artifact is absent from R6 because the expected file is missing, the R6 package index has no `SubstanceReferenceInformation` entry, and exact-package searches found no same-name reference. Confidence is medium for successor analysis because `SubstanceDefinition` is a plausible domain successor, but the supplied inputs do not include an official diff or ConceptMap confirming the intended migration path.

findings.title: SubstanceReferenceInformation resource is absent from the R6 core package

oldState.summary: R4 defines a concrete SubstanceReferenceInformation resource.
oldState.narrativeMd: The R4 package index and assigned StructureDefinition define `SubstanceReferenceInformation` as a concrete, non-abstract resource with canonical URL `http://hl7.org/fhir/StructureDefinition/SubstanceReferenceInformation`, `kind: resource`, `type: SubstanceReferenceInformation`, and base `DomainResource`.

newState.summary: No R6 StructureDefinition for SubstanceReferenceInformation was found.
newState.narrativeMd: The expected R6 file is absent and the R6 package index contains no `SubstanceReferenceInformation` entry. The only R6 substance resources found in the index are `Substance` and `SubstanceDefinition`, neither of which has the old id, type, or canonical URL.

facts.note: The R4 file exists; the corresponding R6 filename does not.
No R6 package index entry with this canonical URL was found.
R6 retains a substance domain but not this resource identity.
The artifact was immature in R4, but removal is still instance-breaking for adopters.

structuredDelta.matchingRationaleMd: The old artifact was matched by exact id, type, filename, and canonical URL. No exact R6 match was present, and candidate domain resources do not preserve the old identity.

impact.impactRationaleMd: FHIR resource identity is encoded directly in serialized instances through `resourceType`. An R4 instance with `resourceType: "SubstanceReferenceInformation"` has no R6 core StructureDefinition to validate against. R6 code generators, serializers, validators, and REST endpoint dispatch tables based on the core package will generally not include this resource type.
impact.safetyOrBusinessRiskMd: The resource was R4 draft/trial-use and FMM 0, suggesting limited deployment, but systems that did adopt it may lose access to regulatory or substance reference data unless they preserve a compatibility path.

justification.inferredGoal: Retire or consolidate an immature substance reference-information resource into the redesigned substance definition model.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Keep a deprecated R6 compatibility resource preserving the R4 shape while steering new implementations to SubstanceDefinition.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: The inferred goal--retiring or consolidating a very low-maturity, sparsely defined R4 substance resource into the R6 substance model--is reasonable. A less-breaking base design was possible, but it would have required R6 to keep the old resource identity as a deprecated compatibility surface. Given the R4 artifact's `Todo.` definitions and FMM 0/trial-use status, carrying that surface forward would impose material long-term model and implementation cost, so the break is probably justified rather than clearly avoidable.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: The best base-design alternative would have been to retain `SubstanceReferenceInformation` in R6 with its R4 content model, mark it deprecated, and direct new use to `SubstanceDefinition`. That would preserve old `resourceType` validation and generated-model compatibility. The tradeoff is significant: R6 would keep a poorly specified legacy resource alongside the replacement substance model, creating duplicate same-domain representations that may never disappear.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: Preserves R4 instances but leaves an under-specified FMM0 resource in core and risks indefinite duplicate substance representations.

evidence.detail: R4 defines `SubstanceReferenceInformation` as a non-abstract resource specialization of DomainResource.
No R6 package index entry exists for `SubstanceReferenceInformation`.
Exact search of the R6 package found no occurrences of `SubstanceReferenceInformation`.
R6 substance-domain resource StructureDefinitions in the index are `Substance` and `SubstanceDefinition`.

oldValidNewInvalidJson.comment: Legacy reference information recorded against a substance.

examples.examplesMd: The example is intentionally minimal. The breaking mechanism is the resource identity: without an R6 StructureDefinition for this `resourceType`, even otherwise simple R4 content is not a valid R6 core resource.

findings.narrativeMd: `SubstanceReferenceInformation` was removed from the R6 core resource set rather than preserved under the same canonical identity. This is a hard break for any R4 data, parsers, generated classes, validators, or API contracts that mention the resource by name. It is not an inherited base-resource change; it is local to this artifact's presence in the core package.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: An R4 instance with `resourceType: "SubstanceReferenceInformation"` can be valid against the R4 package but has no R6 resource definition to validate against. Strict R6 validators should reject the resource as unknown unless an implementation-specific compatibility profile or extension mechanism is introduced. This finding is primarily R4-to-R6; there is no direct R6-to-R4 counterpart because R6 does not define the resource.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Inventory stored resources and code references by `resourceType`. If data must be preserved, choose an explicit strategy: retain an R4 compatibility store, transform selected fields into `SubstanceDefinition` with project-specific rules, or carry the original content in extensions/provenance. Generated clients should remove assumptions that an R6 core model contains a `SubstanceReferenceInformation` class.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: The removal may be justified by the R4 artifact's low maturity and sparse `Todo.` definitions, but the backward-compatible alternative was straightforward: keep a deprecated resource shell or publish an official cross-version mapping. That alternative would reduce validation and codegen breakage while allowing the substance model to evolve.

freshReview.narrativeMd: `SubstanceReferenceInformation` is genuinely absent as an R6 core resource, so an R4 instance carrying that `resourceType` has no base R6 StructureDefinition/class/endpoint to target. That is a real top-level compatibility break for any adopter. The reason I do not rate it as needing renewed design attention is the stability context: the R4 artifact was FMM 0/trial-use, its own local definitions are mostly placeholders, and a targeted search did not surface official IG or vendor evidence of production reliance. Keeping a deprecated legacy resource would be more compatible, but it would make R6 carry an obsolete, under-specified substance model beside the consolidated `SubstanceDefinition` direction.
keyEvidence: R4 StructureDefinition defines `SubstanceReferenceInformation` as a concrete DomainResource with id/type/canonical URL matching the old resource.

The expected R6 StructureDefinition file is absent, exact package search found no `SubstanceReferenceInformation`, and the R6 package index lists substance resources `Substance` and `SubstanceDefinition` instead.
R4 maturity map and StructureDefinition extensions show FMM 0 and trial-use/draft status.
Quick web search of official FHIR IG registry, HL7 materials, and vendor/public documentation found no documented production use or official IG dependency.
freshReview.fmmEffect: FMM 0/trial-use substantially softens the stability expectation. The break is real, but low maturity plus lack of quick production-use evidence keeps it from being disproportionate on compatibility grounds alone.
freshReview.compatibilityMechanism: old-valid/new-invalid, runtime/API/codegen: an R4 `resourceType: SubstanceReferenceInformation` instance is unknown to base R6 validators, generated models, serializers, and REST dispatch tables.
freshReview.lessBreakingAlternativeAssessment: A less-breaking base design exists in principle: retain a deprecated `SubstanceReferenceInformation` resource shell or transitional legacy resource while steering new content to `SubstanceDefinition`. The tradeoff is material for an FMM 0 artifact because it preserves a largely placeholder, duplicative resource identity and forces R6 tooling/search/codegen to support a model the substance domain appears to have consolidated away.
freshReview.comparisonToExisting: partially agree with the existing hard-break assessment, because the resource removal is a direct R4-to-R6 break. I would soften the practical impact relative to the existing High framing because the FMM 0/trial-use status and lack of documented production use make the removal more acceptable; the existing report also did not count a less-breaking alternative even though a deprecated shell is possible but costly.

findings.title: R4 local content model has no lossless R6 successor mapping

oldState.summary: R4 local content consists of optional `comment`, `gene`, `geneElement`, `classification`, and `target` elements.
oldState.narrativeMd: The R4 resource has five top-level local elements after inherited DomainResource content. The backbone groups are all optional and repeating except `comment`, and their child definitions are mostly `Todo.` with no local terminology bindings.

newState.summary: No same-path R6 elements exist; candidate SubstanceDefinition has a different substance model.
newState.narrativeMd: `SubstanceDefinition` includes broad substance description elements such as `identifier`, `classification`, `domain`, `description`, `note`, `moiety`, `characterization`, `property`, `structure`, `code`, `name`, `relationship`, and `sourceMaterial`. It does not contain same-name `gene`, `geneElement`, or `target` elements and is not a direct renamed form of `SubstanceReferenceInformation`.

facts.note: No R6 `SubstanceReferenceInformation` local content model exists.
Exact names were not present as elements in the reviewed R6 `SubstanceDefinition` resource.
Overlap is partial and semantic, not a confirmed same-element mapping.
R6 `SubstanceDefinition` is broader than the old assigned resource and cannot round-trip through it.

structuredDelta.matchingRationaleMd: `SubstanceDefinition` was selected only as a candidate because it is the R6 substance-domain resource with detailed substance definition semantics. The field-level match is weak: several R4 sections have no same-name or same-shape R6 counterpart.

impact.impactRationaleMd: The resource removal already makes R4 instances invalid in R6. Beyond validation, there is a separate conversion risk: local R4 content cannot be moved mechanically into `SubstanceDefinition` without choosing semantics. Conversely, valid R6 `SubstanceDefinition` content is much broader than the old `SubstanceReferenceInformation` model and is not cleanly representable in that R4 resource.
impact.safetyOrBusinessRiskMd: If the resource was used for regulatory substance knowledge, an incorrect map could lose gene/target meaning or misclassify relationship information. The risk is project-specific because R4 adoption was probably low.

justification.inferredGoal: Consolidate substance reference information into a more complete substance definition model.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: The base-design alternative is retaining the old resource or another legacy compatibility surface; maps and extensions alone are migration mitigations, not backward-compatible base R6 design.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: A richer `SubstanceDefinition` model is a reasonable R6 goal, and the R4 local model is weakly specified. The existing report's mapping-and-extension path should not be counted as a `Yes` base-design alternative because ordinary StructureMaps, ConceptMaps, or cross-version extensions do not make R4 instances valid R6 base resources. Preserving the old local content in base R6 would require a deprecated resource or equivalent legacy surface, which has material interoperability and maintenance tradeoffs; with those tradeoffs, the breaking redesign is probably justified.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: A less-breaking base R6 design could have retained `SubstanceReferenceInformation` with its `comment`, `gene`, `geneElement`, `classification`, and `target` content, possibly deprecated and linked to `SubstanceDefinition`. Adding conversion maps or extensions would still be useful, but those are mitigations rather than the base alternative. The compatibility-resource approach would preserve old content most completely, but it would also keep a parallel legacy representation for substance reference information and could confuse validators, code generators, and implementers choosing between old and new shapes.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: Reduces data loss for legacy records but creates duplicated substance-model structures, validation ambiguity, and ongoing implementation burden.

evidence.detail: R4 local top-level elements are `comment`, `gene`, `geneElement`, `classification`, and `target`.
The candidate R6 resource has a different local content model and no same-name `gene`, `geneElement`, or `target` elements.
Searches did not identify these R4 local element names as R6 substance-model successors.

examples.examplesMd: The fragments are illustrative. The R4 fragment shows local sections that have no same-path R6 target. The R6 fragment shows normal `SubstanceDefinition` concepts that cannot be represented by the old `SubstanceReferenceInformation` content model.

findings.narrativeMd: The local model did not survive as a direct R6 model. This matters even if a system accepts the resource removal, because migration cannot be done by changing only `resourceType`. The old content must be interpreted and remodeled, and some sections likely need extensions or manual curation.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: Validation fails at the resource level in R6. If an implementation tries to migrate into `SubstanceDefinition`, field-level compatibility is not guaranteed: some R4 fields have no R6 base element, and many R6 `SubstanceDefinition` fields have no R4 `SubstanceReferenceInformation` representation. This affects generated classes, transformation code, database schemas, and round-trip tests.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Do not implement a blind one-to-one transform. First classify each R4 record by which local sections are populated. Map simple descriptive comments only if the project accepts a target such as `SubstanceDefinition.description` or `note`; map classification only after verifying semantics; preserve gene/geneElement/target details in extensions or external references unless an official mapping is obtained. Test for loss by round-tripping representative records.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: A backward-compatible alternative was available through a migration supplement: explicit StructureMap rules for shared concepts, cross-version extensions for removed concepts, and warnings for lossy sections. This would allow HL7 to redesign the R6 substance model while giving implementers an auditable path for legacy R4 data.
findings.reviewerNotesMd: The candidate-successor analysis should be reviewed by a substance-domain expert. The package evidence supports `SubstanceDefinition` as a likely consolidation target, but not a confirmed replacement for every R4 local section.

freshReview.narrativeMd: The R4 local content model did not survive as a same-shape R6 model: optional `comment`, `gene`, `geneElement`, `classification`, and `target` content cannot be migrated merely by renaming the resource. A system with populated records would need a domain-specific transformation, and some gene/target meaning could be lost or require extensions. Still, these R4 fields are optional, very under-specified, and attached to an FMM 0/trial-use artifact with no quick evidence of broad deployment. For base R6, replacing the draft local model with the broader `SubstanceDefinition` model looks proportionate even though it leaves legacy adopters with migration work.
keyEvidence: R4 local top-level elements are `comment`, `gene`, `geneElement`, `classification`, and `target`; their local definitions and shorts are mostly `Todo.` and they have no local terminology bindings.

R6 `SubstanceDefinition` has a different top-level model including `identifier`, `status`, `classification`, `domain`, `description`, `note`, `moiety`, `characterization`, `property`, `structure`, `code`, `name`, `relationship`, and `sourceMaterial`.
R6 package searches found no same-name `gene`, `geneElement`, `target`, `geneSequenceOrigin`, `organismType`, or `amountType` successor paths.
Quick web search found no official IG or public production-use evidence that would raise the legacy mapping burden.
freshReview.fmmEffect: FMM 0/trial-use softens the concern; the mapping gap matters for adopters with data, but the low maturity and placeholder definitions argue against preserving every old local section in base R6.
freshReview.compatibilityMechanism: R6-to-R4 loss and migration/API-codegen burden: the old resource-level validation failure is covered by the root finding; this finding is mainly about non-lossless transformation and changed generated data models for local fields.
freshReview.lessBreakingAlternativeAssessment: R6 could have kept the old resource or added deprecated legacy backbones to `SubstanceDefinition`, but that would duplicate an under-specified local model and require precedence/mapping rules. StructureMaps, extensions, or migration guidance would mitigate adopter pain but are not themselves less-breaking base R6 designs.
freshReview.comparisonToExisting: partially agree that a blind lossless successor mapping is not supported by the package evidence. I would temper the existing High impact because the affected content is FMM 0, optional, sparsely defined, and not shown to be in production; no low-cost base alternative is evident.

findings.title: Candidate mapping of target amount/interaction data changes type domain and required context

oldState.summary: R4 target amount is optional and allows Quantity, Range, or string.
oldState.narrativeMd: `SubstanceReferenceInformation.target` models a target with optional `target` Identifier, `type`, `interaction`, `organism`, `organismType`, `amount[x]`, `amountType`, and source references.

newState.summary: The closest reviewed candidate is SubstanceDefinition.relationship, whose amount allows Quantity, Ratio, or string and whose relationship type is mandatory.
newState.narrativeMd: `SubstanceDefinition.relationship` is a link between this substance and another substance definition or code. It requires `relationship.type` (`1..1`) and is semantically different from an R4 target/interaction record.

facts.note: This is a candidate mapping comparison, not a direct same-path element comparison.
R4 target amount ranges would need another representation if mapped to the candidate R6 relationship amount.
R6 ratio amounts would not round-trip through the R4 target amount choice.
A migration to `relationship` may require selecting a relationship type even when R4 only supplied target interaction details.

structuredDelta.matchingRationaleMd: The match is speculative and based on similar amount/source concepts, not on a confirmed rename. The semantic mismatch is itself the risk.

impact.impactRationaleMd: If implementers map R4 `target` records to R6 `SubstanceDefinition.relationship`, valid R4 `Range` amounts have no direct candidate type and R6 `Ratio` amounts have no R4 target amount type. The mandatory R6 `relationship.type` can also force a semantic choice absent from some R4 data.
impact.safetyOrBusinessRiskMd: Incorrect target/relationship mapping could change the meaning of pharmacologic or biological interaction information. The clinical/business impact depends on whether systems used these draft fields.

justification.inferredGoal: Represent quantitative substance relationships in a more structured substance definition model.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: No calibrated base-design alternative applies to this candidate-only comparison; Range/Ratio handling is migration guidance unless `relationship` is confirmed as the successor.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: This finding compares R4 `target.amount[x]` with a speculative `SubstanceDefinition.relationship.amount[x]` migration target, not a confirmed same-path R4-to-R6 base element. The core base-design break is the removed resource identity and local model, covered by the other findings. Because the evidence does not establish that `relationship` was intended as the successor for `target`, the reasonableness of the R6 type choice cannot be assessed as the justification for a direct breaking change.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: Not applicable as a calibrated base-design alternative. If implementers choose to map R4 target records to `SubstanceDefinition.relationship`, then transform rules, extensions, or perhaps a wider amount choice could mitigate Range/Ratio loss. Those are candidate migration choices, not proof that R6 should have changed its base `relationship.amount[x]` design, and they would not by themselves make R4 `SubstanceReferenceInformation` instances valid in R6.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: Adding `Range` or legacy target fields to `SubstanceDefinition` would broaden relationship semantics and still would not preserve R4 resource instances by itself.

examples.examplesMd: These examples isolate the choice-type mismatch. They are not complete migration recommendations and depend on choosing `SubstanceDefinition.relationship` as the target.

findings.narrativeMd: The most tempting candidate for some R4 `target` quantitative data is `SubstanceDefinition.relationship`, but that is not a safe mechanical mapping. The choice types differ and the R6 candidate carries relationship semantics that the R4 target backbone does not require.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: This is not a direct same-path R6 validation break because the old resource is gone. It becomes a concrete compatibility problem when converting data: R4 range-valued target amounts cannot be placed into the candidate R6 amount choice without a lossy transform or extension, and R6 ratio-valued relationship amounts cannot be represented in the R4 target amount choice.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: If target data is populated, require a domain review before mapping it to `SubstanceDefinition.relationship`. Define explicit rules for `Range` and `Ratio`, decide how to populate mandatory relationship type, and preserve the original R4 target record when no unambiguous mapping exists.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: A broader candidate amount choice or official cross-version extension would reduce loss. Because the R4 field was draft and under-specified, R6 may have chosen a cleaner relationship model, but conversion guidance is still needed for adopters.
findings.reviewerNotesMd: This finding is intentionally marked as candidate-only. It should not be read as proof that HL7 intended `target` to map to `relationship`.

freshReview.narrativeMd: The type-domain mismatch is real if an implementer maps R4 `target` records into R6 `SubstanceDefinition.relationship`: R4 `target.amount[x]` permits `Range`, while the candidate R6 `relationship.amount[x]` permits `Ratio`, and R6 also requires `relationship.type`. The limiting issue is that this is a candidate-only mapping, not a confirmed rename or successor path. Without official mapping rationale, it is not possible to say whether R6 intentionally replaced target amounts with relationship amounts, whether another R6 representation is intended, or whether the correct answer is preservation outside the base model. Low FMM keeps this from being a revisit-level concern, but the path-specific compatibility judgment remains uncertain.
keyEvidence: R4 `SubstanceReferenceInformation.target.amount[x]` is 0..1 with choice types `Quantity`, `Range`, and `string`.
R6 candidate `SubstanceDefinition.relationship.amount[x]` is 0..1 with choice types `Quantity`, `Ratio`, and `string`.
R6 candidate `SubstanceDefinition.relationship.type` is mandatory 1..1 with example binding to substance relationship type.
The existing report itself marks the target-to-relationship comparison as candidate-only with low match confidence; package searches did not identify a same-name R6 target amount successor.
freshReview.fmmEffect: FMM 0/trial-use softens the stability concern and argues against treating the conditional type mismatch as a design flaw by itself. If real regulatory/scientific target data exists, expert mapping risk remains, but no quick production-use evidence was found.
freshReview.compatibilityMechanism: unknown, with possible R6-to-R4 loss: the concrete problem appears only under an unconfirmed `target` to `relationship` migration; then `Range` and `Ratio` values and mandatory relationship type can require lossy or expert mapping.
freshReview.lessBreakingAlternativeAssessment: If `relationship` is the intended successor, widening `relationship.amount[x]` to include `Range` or defining a base legacy extension could preserve more R4 data, but that may undermine the R6 relationship model and does not address the mandatory relationship-type semantics. If `relationship` is not the intended successor, the alternative assessment changes entirely; official mapping evidence is needed.
freshReview.comparisonToExisting: partially agree with the existing Medium potential-impact finding that the candidate paths do not round-trip cleanly. I do not fully agree with treating it as a settled type-domain break because the successor mapping is speculative and the low-FMM source content weakens the case for base-model preservation.

checkedNoMaterialChange.notesMd: The R4 local `SubstanceReferenceInformation` elements have no explicit local terminology bindings, so no old required/extensible binding was narrowed or removed on a same-path local element. Candidate `SubstanceDefinition` bindings are new-model concerns rather than direct same-element changes.

No local, artifact-specific invariants were found on the R4 local content beyond common `ele-1`/`ext-1` style constraints inherited through base element patterns. Because the R6 artifact is absent, same-path constraint comparison is not applicable.

R4 local source references target `DocumentReference`. R6 `SubstanceDefinition` also has several `DocumentReference` source fields, but they are not same-path successors, so no direct local reference-target narrowing was counted.
No fixed value, pattern value, or default value constraints were identified on the R4 local `SubstanceReferenceInformation` content model.
No local `maxLength`, regex, minValue, or maxValue restrictions were identified on the R4 local elements.
No local slicing rules were identified on the R4 local content model.

No substantive R4 local element such as `comment`, `gene`, `geneElement`, `classification`, `target`, or their data children is marked `isModifier`. `modifierExtension` handling is inherited/base infrastructure and is out of scope.

There is no R6 same-path content model to compare. The material cardinality issue is therefore the artifact-level removal; candidate `SubstanceDefinition` mandatory elements such as `property.type`, `molecularWeight.amount`, `name.name`, and `relationship.type` were not counted as same-element cardinality changes.
R4 local elements are generally marked summary, but no R6 same-path elements exist. Summary-flag changes in inherited elements are out of scope.

nonBreakingNotableChanges.title: R4 artifact was low maturity and under-specified; R6 candidate model is more mature
nonBreakingNotableChanges.whyNotBreakingMd: Maturity/status metadata and sparse `Todo.` definitions do not themselves make an instance invalid. The breaking issue is the artifact's absence from R6, reported separately.
nonBreakingNotableChanges.migrationAwarenessMd: The R4 trial-use/FMM 0 status explains why adopters should expect manual review. `SubstanceDefinition` is active and marked normative in the R6 package extensions, but it is not a direct identity-equivalent replacement.

nonBreakingNotableChanges.title: R6 substance resource family is smaller in the package index
nonBreakingNotableChanges.whyNotBreakingMd: This is contextual evidence rather than a separate local break for `SubstanceReferenceInformation`; the local break is already captured as removal of the assigned artifact.
nonBreakingNotableChanges.migrationAwarenessMd: R4 indexed multiple specialized substance resources, while R6 indexed `Substance` and `SubstanceDefinition`. Migration planning should consider the broader substance model, not only this removed resource.

followUpDependencies.reasonMd: `SubstanceDefinition` is the closest reviewed R6 substance-domain successor candidate and needs its own detailed R4/R6 assessment before automated migration rules are finalized.

followUpDependencies.nameOrUrl: R4 SubstanceReferenceInformation to R6 SubstanceDefinition/Substance cross-version mapping
followUpDependencies.reasonMd: An official ConceptMap or StructureMap would resolve whether the candidate mappings in this report are intended and where unmapped gene/target content should go.
Inherited base-resource differences, including common element bindings and constraints, were intentionally excluded from local findings and should be handled by the base artifact reports.

analysisLimitations.descriptionMd: The local packages did not provide an official R4-to-R6 diff explaining whether `SubstanceReferenceInformation` was removed, merged, or intentionally replaced by `SubstanceDefinition`.
analysisLimitations.whatWouldResolveItMd: An HL7 change note, ballot reconciliation note, or official diff for the substance model.

analysisLimitations.descriptionMd: No authoritative ConceptMap or StructureMap was available to confirm the intended target for `comment`, `gene`, `geneElement`, `classification`, or `target` content.
